title: Ge/ZnS Periodic Quarter-Wave Stack with 8 Pairs
scientific_hypothesis: A Ge/ZnS alternating quarter-wave stack with 8 pairs (16 finite layers) on CaF2 substrate will produce measurable transmittance peaks in the 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands while demonstrating stopband behavior in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm, with valid candidates surviving material data verification.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack design using high-index Ge and low-index ZnS provides strong index contrast for efficient Bragg reflection in stopbands. Computational optimization adjusts individual layer thicknesses from quarter-wave baseline to split the primary passband into two transmission windows.
proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | (Ge/ZnS)_8 | Air, totaling 16 finite dielectric layers
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 16 layers
optimization starting from quarter-wave thickness at 4.45 μm center wavelength
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands
maintain total layer count at exactly 16
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Bragg reflectors
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS pair has documented mid-IR optical constants in evidence
Reduced layer count (16 vs 24) eliminates potential buffer overflow
High index contrast enables strong stopband blocking with fewer layers
known_risks: Single periodic stack may not achieve dual-band separation without cavity defects
Ge absorption may increase at longer wavelengths beyond 5 μm
Quarter-wave baseline may require significant optimization to split passband
execution_request_english: Design and optimize a periodic dielectric multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for normal incidence. Use Germanium (Ge) as high-index material and Zinc Sulfide (ZnS) as low-index material. Stack topology: CaF2 | (Ge/ZnS)_8 | Air, totaling exactly 16 finite dielectric layers. Initialize all layers at quarter-wave optical thickness centered at 4.45 μm. Optimize all 16 layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in two passbands (4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm) while minimizing transmittance in two stopbands (3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm). No metal layers. Evaluate at wavelengths 3600-5200 nm. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all valid candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Changed from Si3N4/MgF2 to Ge/ZnS material pair due to material_data failure in route_03. Ge/ZnS is explicitly documented in evidence for mid-IR filters. Reduced layer count from maximum to 16 layers to rule out stack-length buffer issues.
